title: Disrupted Initialization with Simulated Annealing to Break 120 nm Clustering
scientific_hypothesis: The 120 nm thickness clustering in prior iterations represents a local minimum artifact from bound-constrained gradient descent. Randomly reinitializing layers previously pinned at 120 nm within a 30-150 nm window, followed by simulated annealing optimization, will escape this local minimum and achieve higher dual-band performance.
design_principle: Disrupt symmetric thickness clustering by random reinitialization of bound-saturated layers, then use simulated annealing's temperature-dependent acceptance probability to explore broader thickness space before converging.
proposed_topology: 24 alternating layers starting with HfO2 on substrate, ending with SiO2 at air interface. Exact sequence: Substrate | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Air
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 800-1500 nm band
Maximize mean reflectance in 200-400 nm band
Maintain robustness under ±15 nm thickness tolerance
manufacturing_considerations: Thickness bounds 30-150 nm compatible with standard deposition control
HfO2/SiO2 material pair well-established for space optics
theory_basis: Needle optimization technique for non-quarter-wave designs (evidence: CorpusId:225461372)
Evolutionary optimization with selection/mutation/crossover operations (evidence: CorpusId:243942968)
HfO2/SiO2 heterostructure refractive index contrast enables interference filtering (evidence: CorpusId:254823355)
expected_advantages: Breaks local minimum trapping from prior gradient-only optimization
Simulated annealing explores broader solution space
Maintains proven 24-layer topology while improving thickness distribution
known_risks: Simulated annealing may require more iterations to converge
Random initialization may temporarily reduce target score before improvement
No guarantee of finding global optimum
execution_request_english: Optimize a 24-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Layer sequence: HfO2/SiO2 repeated 12 times (24 total finite layers). Initialize all layer thicknesses uniformly random within 30-150 nm range. Use simulated annealing optimizer with initial temperature 0.1, cooling rate 0.95, minimum temperature 0.001. Optimize thicknesses to maximize mean transmittance in 800-1500 nm band and mean reflectance in 200-400 nm band at normal incidence, unpolarized light. Apply ±15 nm absolute normal thickness tolerance for robustness evaluation. Total layer count fixed at 24. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 200-400 nm, 800-1500 nm. soft objectives: High transmission in 800-1500 nm band; High reflection in 200-400 nm band. behaviors to suppress or avoid: Low transmission in 200-400 nm band; Low reflection in 800-1500 nm band. manufacturing constraints: Total layers <= 30; Materials limited to HfO2 and SiO2.
revision_reason: Directly addresses feedback directive to disrupt the '120 nm backbone' artifact by reinitializing all layers within broader 30-150 nm window and switching from gradient descent to simulated annealing to escape local minima.
